column1: # Svehla, R. A. (1962). Estimated viscosities and thermal conductivities of gases at
# high temperatures. NASA Technical Report R-132 (Lewis Research Center).
# US government work -- public domain (no licence to honour; cite the primary).
# Table I(a) "Force constants for molecules", report pages 20-24 = PDF pages 22-26 of
# thirdParty/svehla/NASA-TR-R-132-Svehla-1962.pdf.  Table I(b) (method legend) is on report
# page 25 = PDF page 27 -- see svehla1962_methods.txt beside this file.
# Every value below was READ FROM THE PAGE IMAGE (pdftoppm at 300 dpi, horizontal
# slices); the pdftotext dump was used only to locate the pages.  `verified` is
# `image` for every row; a row that could not be read would say `unreadable` with
# empty values (there are none).  sigma in angstrom [A], epsilon/k in kelvin [K],
# exactly as printed (no rounding, no unit conversion).  methodSigma / methodEps are
# Svehla's Table I(b) codes: 1-4 rest on EXPERIMENTAL transport data (1 = least-squares
# fit of viscosity data; 2 = graphical, viscosity; 3 = least-squares, thermal
# conductivity; 4 = graphical, thermal conductivity); 5-23 are ESTIMATES.
# svehlaDataPage = Svehla's column "Page (b)": the report page of his calculated
# transport-property table for that molecule.  refsAsPrinted = his bibliography
# numbers (his column "Experimental viscosity data references", or, on report page
# 24 for the five repeated noble gases, "Experimental thermal conductivity data
# references" -- `refsColumn` says which).
# moleculeAsPrinted keeps Svehla's typography (subscripts flattened: CCl4, n-C4H10,
# iso-C4H10, cyclo-C3H6, B(OCH3)3, C(CH3)4).  Ar, He, Kr, Ne and Xe appear TWICE:
# once from viscosity data (report pages 20-23) and once from thermal-conductivity
# data (report page 24, methods 3/4/22).
